name: nanofuzz
description: NaNofuzz is a fast and easy-to-use automatic test suite generator for TypeScript and Python that runs inside VS Code
author: The NaNofuzz Team @ Carnegie Mellon University

languageModelTools.name: nanofuzz_listTargets
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Discovers and lists all exported functions (synchronous and asynchronous), type signatures, parameter structures, and ready-to-use property validator and input transformer code templates (validatorTemplate and transformerTemplate) in a TypeScript or Python source file that can be targeted for structure-aware fuzzing and property testing. Functions under test with preconditions can be paired with an exported input transformer using assume(condition) or raise/throw UnsatisfiedAssumption(msg) to filter out invalid or out-of-domain inputs from the fuzzing loop. If a target function is not exported or uses unsupported signature types, you can write an exported wrapper function with type annotations in its signature that calls the target function, and list or test that wrapper function instead.

filePath.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the source file (e.g. src/math.ts or test.py).

languageModelTools.name: nanofuzz_fuzzFunction
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Runs coverage-guided, structure-aware property fuzzing on a target function (synchronous or asynchronous) in TypeScript or Python. Uses dynamic branch-coverage feedback loops, type-aware/grammar generation, coverage-directed mutation, AI input generation, and automated input shrinking (minimization) to find minimal counterexamples, crashes, and edge cases. Returns synthesized executable regression tests (Jest or Pytest) and branch coverage metrics. To filter invalid inputs or express preconditions, write an exported transformer function (<fn>Transformer) using assume(condition) or UnsatisfiedAssumption. If a target function is not exported, is a class method, or uses unsupported signature types, you can write an exported wrapper function with type annotations in its signature that calls the target, and fuzz that wrapper function instead.

filePath.description: Absolute or workspace-relative path to the source file containing the target function.

functionName.description: The exact name of the exported function to test.

model.description: The language model name or family currently used by the calling agent (e.g. 'gemini-2.0-flash', 'gemini-3.7-flash', 'claude-3.5-sonnet', 'gpt-4o'). Always pass your own model name or family here so NaNofuzz uses the same AI model for input generation.

vendor.description: The language model vendor/provider identifier currently used by the calling agent (e.g. 'google', 'copilot', 'gemini', 'openai'). Always pass your active vendor/provider so NaNofuzz routes queries to the exact same provider account and billing.

maxTests.description: Maximum number of test cases to generate and execute (default: 1000).

timeoutMs.description: Maximum suite execution timeout in milliseconds (default: 3000).

maxFailures.description: Maximum number of failures to find before stopping (default: 0 for no limit).

seed.description: Optional pseudo-random generator seed for deterministic fuzzing runs.

inputs.description: Optional list of concrete seed inputs to test, expressed as objects mapping parameter names to argument values (e.g. [{"name": "Alice", "age": 30}]). Useful for targeting specific uncovered branches or edge cases.

items.description: Object mapping parameter names to argument values.

tests.description: Optional list of unit test specifications with inputs and expected outcomes. Each test specifies 'input' (parameter object or argument array), plus optional 'expectedOutput' (expected return value), 'expectedException' (boolean), or 'expectedTimeout' (boolean). When expected outcomes are provided, NaNofuzz validates them with its Example Oracle and synthesizes direct unit assertions in reproducer tests.

input.description: Object mapping parameter names to argument values.

expectedOutput.description: The expected return value of the function for these inputs.

expectedException.description: True if an exception or error is expected to be thrown for these inputs.

expectedTimeout.description: True if a timeout is expected for these inputs.

nanofuzz.generators.scheduler.impl.title: Composite generator scheduler algorithm
enumDescriptions: Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB): Productivity-weighted selection based on feedback and exploration
Random: Uniform pseudo-random selection among ready generators
Round Robin: Sequential cyclic selection across ready generators
Upper Confidence Bound (UCB1) algorithm balancing empirical yield and exploration uncertainty
Thompson Sampling (Bayesian Bandit) drawing from posterior productivity distributions
Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA): Fast O(1) rolling productivity updates
MOpt (Particle Swarm Optimization): Multi-particle swarm moving through probability space
nanofuzz.generators.scheduler.impl.description: Scheduler used by CompositeInputGenerator to pick the next input generator
